## Bottom line

The five commits after `e80bcf156` are individually competent — real bugs, real fixes, tests attached to almost every one — but the batch as a whole is not converging, and it's being validated almost entirely by AI reviewers rather than by CI. The newest commit introduced a reproducible P1 bug in a file it created two commits earlier.

The range is `8d595357c → 8a1cfe72c → b688bba03 → 2f6f5fb09 → e4c7cb580`, +1541/−199 across 46 files, of which 595 added lines are tests.

## What's good

The fixes address genuine problems rather than cosmetics. Private content is now excluded from generated `llms.txt` artifacts, OpenAPI sources are checked for cycles before `JSON.stringify` writes `manifest.json`, RSS item links are clamped to the site origin, and TypeScript configs are transpiled to a real temp file instead of a `data:` URL so that relative imports inside a config actually resolve. The `--no-blog` CLI flag was reading `options.noBlog` when CAC exposes it as `options.blog === false`, so the documented flag was a no-op; that's fixed and the narrowed React/Svelte peer ranges were correctly propagated into `package-lock.json`.

There's real deduplication too: `isDocsContentProtected` was lifted out of `search.ts` and reused in `llms.ts`, and the two hand-rolled fence scanners in `sanitize.ts` and `compat/fumadocs.ts` were replaced by a shared `markdown-fences.ts`.

I built the workspace and ran the suite at the head commit: 188 tests pass across 19 files, including the 26 in `markdown.test.ts` and 17 in `compile.test.ts` that cover the new code. The hand-rolled anchor-tag parser in `links.ts` is genuinely well tested — `data-href` decoys, `>` inside quoted attribute values, unterminated tags.

## What's wrong

**The newest commit shipped a P1 in `markdown-fences.ts`, the file introduced two commits earlier.** I reproduced it. When a fenced code block sits inside a list item and its *content* contains a line that looks like a nested list opening a fence, the scanner accepts that content line as the closer and then re-opens a fence on the real closer — inverting in-fence state for the entire rest of the document:

```
inFence=0 fenceLine=0 | "- Example:"
inFence=1 fenceLine=1 | "  ```js"
inFence=1 fenceLine=1 | "  - ```"      <- content line treated as closer
inFence=0 fenceLine=0 | "  const x = 1;"  <- real code treated as prose
inFence=1 fenceLine=1 | "  ```"        <- real closer re-opens a fence
inFence=1 fenceLine=0 | "<script>alert(1)</script>"  <- rest of doc is "inside" a fence
```

Downstream, the Fumadocs transform silently stops working on that document — imports aren't stripped and `<Tabs>` isn't rewritten, where the same document without the pathological line transforms correctly. The sanitizer still catches the `<script>` via its independent `collectRawHtml` path, so this isn't a security hole, but it's a correctness regression in new code.

**The sanitizer has a verified detection gap.** `BLOCKED_HTML_PATTERNS` uses `/\son[a-z]+\s*=/i`, which requires whitespace before the handler, so `findUnsafeHtml('<svg/onload=alert(1)>')` returns `[]`. `EVENT_ATTR_RE` in `markdown.ts` makes the same assumption. I probed the render paths and the payload comes out HTML-escaped in all of them, so the reviewer's claim that it executes doesn't reproduce — but `assertSafeSource` will happily pass a document containing it, which is not what that function advertises.

**Copy-paste that the refactor was supposed to eliminate.** `compat/fumadocs.ts` has two consecutive branches with byte-identical bodies (`if (inFence && isFenceLine)` then `if (inFence)`). The ~35-line backtick-run scanner in `sanitize.ts`'s `stripInlineCode` is a near-verbatim duplicate of the one in `rewriteOutsideInlineCode` — written in the same batch that created a shared module specifically to stop duplicating this logic. **It isn't converging.** Codex, cubic, and pullfrog opened five new threads on the head commit `e4c7cb580` — three of them on `markdown-fences.ts`. 52 threads are currently unresolved. Each "close remaining review findings" commit does close real findings, but the rate of new findings isn't dropping.

**Almost nothing is being verified by CI.** The repo's own `ci.yml` has produced zero check runs for the last three commits. The PR is `CONFLICTING` with `dev`, which is the likely reason — GitHub can't build a merge ref, so `pull_request` workflows don't fire. On `8a1cfe72c`, the last commit where CI did run, the JavaScript job failed at `@uifn/examples#build` (unrelated pre-existing breakage) before ever reaching docsfn's test, lint, or typecheck steps, and Docs Guardrails failed on a missing `docs` workspace. CodeRabbit skipped the PR entirely — 560 files against a 100-file limit. So the effective gate is three AI reviewers plus a red Sonar quality gate (new reliability D, new security D, duplication 11.6%).

**Commit messages are boilerplate.** Four of five start with "close remaining review findings for…" and have no body beyond the co-author trailer. ## Verification

The release-gate P1 is real, and I got the literal failure:

```
[release-gate] DOCS_RELEASE_GATE_FAILED: @docsfn/react peerDependencies.react must include ^18.0.0 and ^19.0.0

The 128-character search regression reproduces with the boundary exactly where it says. `8d595357c` changed `edgeNGramMaxLength` from `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` to `128`; querying the indexed token by prefix:

```
len=127 hits=1   len=128 hits=1   len=129 hits=0   len=140 hits=0
```

So a truncated prefix finds the document and the exact full token doesn't.

The sibling-import cache claim reproduces verbatim — I wrote `theme.js` with title `Before`, loaded the config, rewrote it to `After`, reloaded:

```
load #1 title: Before
load #2 title: Before (expected 'After')
```

Notably the PR *has* a test named "loads a TypeScript config that imports a sibling module," but it only asserts two concurrent loads agree; it never edits the sibling. That's precisely the gap.

The dev rebuild loop is the most conditional claim and it was honest about that. I confirmed every ingredient: `chokidar.watch(watchTargets, { ignoreInitial: true })` passes no `ignored` option, `buildFsWatchMetadata` puts `resolve(input.root)` in the watched set, and the `watcher.on("all")` handler only skips paths under `outDir`. Then I tested whether a short-lived dotfile is actually observable:

```
fast (no await):     0 event(s) -> []
slow (250ms await):  2 event(s) -> ["add .docsfn.<hex>.mjs", "unlink .docsfn.<hex>.mjs"]
```

That is exactly the behavior it described, including why the slow config is needed. Each of those two events triggers a rebuild, and each rebuild writes another temp file.

The supporting numbers are also right. 229 tests = 188 core + 16 react + 22 svelte + 3 docs. Churn of 2,226 line-touches commit-by-commit versus 1,740 in the combined diff matches to the digit. Sonar duplication 11.6% and new reliability rating D are current. The only figures I couldn't check are the baselines — "from 10.7%" and "from C" at `e80bcf156` — because Sonar overwrites PR analyses.

## Two calibrations

**The release gate isn't wired into CI.** `docsfn/scripts/release-gate.mjs` is documented in `docsfn/README.md` as a manual step; there's no `gate:docsfn-release` script in the root `package.json`, and `ci.yml` only runs `gate:mcpfn-release`. **The root cause is a contradiction the evaluation doesn't surface.** `@uifn/react@0.0.2` declares peer `react: ">=18.3.0 <20"` and `@uifn/svelte@0.0.2` declares `svelte: ">=5.20.0 <6"`, and both are hard dependencies of the docsfn packages. Its table calls `e4c7cb580` "test-heavy and directionally useful, but incomplete." Downstream, the Fumadocs transform silently stops working on that file.

It also doesn't cover the sanitizer gap (`findUnsafeHtml('<svg/onload=alert(1)>')` returns `[]` because the pattern requires whitespace before the handler), and it cites the 11.6% duplication without saying what causes it — a triplicated `contentSignature` that's byte-identical across two of three example sites, a dead duplicated branch in `compat/fumadocs.ts`, and a duplicated inline-code scanner in `sanitize.ts`.

Tracing the n-gram cap through the review threads shows the failure mode better than any single finding. content.text:
The turbo fix is committed on a new branch off `dev`, and it works — but it does **not** get CI green, because `dev` has five other independent build failures underneath.

## The fix

`c958062f8` on `fix/uifn-examples-turbo-deps`, 6 files, +16/−1.

The diagnosis I gave you last turn was right but incomplete. `@uifn/examples` declared no dependencies while its build script shelled out to four sibling workspace builds, so turbo scheduled it as a leaf and started it immediately. I removed that script — turbo already builds all four sub-workspaces as first-class tasks, so it was pure duplication that hid the dependency edges.

That exposed the same gap one level down. The workbenches import `@uifn/react`, `@uifn/svelte`, `@uifn/solid` and the `@uifn/components-*` bindings without declaring them, and `@uifn/examples-shared` imports `@uifn/core` and `@uifn/registry` without declaring them. I found these by diffing actual `@uifn/*` imports against declared deps, and added the eight missing declarations.

Controlled before/after, same filter, same wiped tree:

```
baseline:  Tasks: 7 successful, 10 total
           Failed: example-react-workbench, example-solid-workbench, example-svelte-workbench

with fix:  Tasks: 20 successful, 20 total
```

The task count doubling is the real tell — turbo now sees the true dependency closure instead of a truncated graph. `npm ci --dry-run` validates the lockfile.

## Why CI still won't go green

I ran `npx turbo run build --continue` across the whole repo to enumerate everything rather than stopping at the first failure. With my fix applied, 213 of 219 tasks pass, and six fail:

`@authfn/docs`, `@filefn/docs`, `@uifn/catalog-svelte`, `@uifn/example-react-playground`, `@uifn/example-svelte-playground`, `superconsole`

These are not ordering problems. I chased `@uifn/example-react-playground` down and it's broken source: `uifn/react/src/generated/breadcrumb.tsx` imports `@uifn/core/primitives/breadcrumb`, and there is no breadcrumb primitive anywhere in `uifn/core/src` — a generated binding for a primitive that was never written. That needs whoever owns uifn, not a config change.

I stopped there rather than continuing. Each layer I fixed revealed another, and I'd moved from "fix turbo ordering" into repairing a subsystem unrelated to docsfn, on someone else's code.

## Where this leaves PR #133

The merge I pushed earlier did its job — the PR is `MERGEABLE` and CI executes. But the `JavaScript` job will keep failing at Build until those six are fixed, so Typecheck, Test, and Lint stay skipped and docsfn still gets no CI signal. My change removes one of the fifteen baseline failures and unblocks the uifn examples specifically; it isn't sufficient on its own.

Worth saying plainly: `dev` is broken independently of PR #133, and no amount of work on that branch will produce a green build.
